newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT-Capel B&K lowers India's HPCL net.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Capel B&K lowers India's HPCL net.

text.p: Securities firm James Capel B&K on Wednesday lowered its 1996/97 (April-March) profit forecast for leading oil firm Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) due to the government delaying a petroleum product price hike.
But the securities firm said it maintained its "buy" recommendation on HPCL as it saw the stock emerging as a favourite in the oil sector.
"HPCL's oil pool dues have risen by 5.0 billion rupees, but that has hardly affected the company's operational performance," analyst Avadhoot Sabnis said in a note to investors.
"However, the delay in the oil price hike will increase financial costs, and we are downgrading our 1996/97 profits by six percent," Sabnis said.
He said HPCL's dues from the oil pool had risen to 12 billion by the end of the fiscal year March 31, 1997.
"These have been financed mainly by short-term borrowing at an average cost of around 12-13 percent."
He pegged his revised net profit figure at 6.14 billion rupees, up from 5.14 billion in 1995/96.
Sabnis said HPCL's growth over the next five years would be funded through internal accruals, already-raised equity and through debt.
"Absence of an impending equity offering should result in better valuation compared with its peers, and we maintain our buy recommendation," he said.
